components.title:
Bonjour ! I'm thrilled to be your Tour Director for your EF tour Paris and Barcelona !
Tour Directors handle all the behind the scenes to make your tour comfortable, smooth pace and enjoyable. Syncing all logistics; from hotel check-in to bus transfers, and everything in between; cultural activities, venue visits, museums entrances, sightseeing with official local guides, walking tours, hotel stays and included EF dinners.

With so many incredible sights to see and only so many hours in the day, every minute counts! To make sure we can enjoy everything at a relaxed pace without missing a beat, please be mindful of our schedule. Staying on top of wake-up calls and departure times helps the whole group have a seamless, stress-free experience.

12.15pm Arrival Paris ORLY airport / 1.45pm Bus transfer ~1h15 drive to Paris
Luggage will remain on the bus until we check into the hotel

PARIS LATIN QUARTER walking tour / free time
The historic heart of intellectual Paris, the Latin Quarter is famous for its winding medieval streets, lively atmosphere, and the presence of the Sorbonne University. Originally named because students and scholars here spoke Latin until the French Revolution, the area is now a vibrant hub of bookstores, quaint cafes, and the Pantheon, offering a glimpse into the bohemian soul of the city.

components.title:
PARIS NOTRE-DAME CATHEDRAL No guided / visit on your own
A masterpiece of French Gothic architecture, Notre-Dame de Paris stands majestically on the Île de la Cité. Although currently undergoing restoration following the 2019 fire, its iconic twin towers and intricate facade remain a symbol of Paris’s resilience and history. It is world-renowned for its stunning stained-glass rose windows, flying buttresses, and its role as the setting for Victor Hugo’s famous novel.

components.title: Lunch free time

ORSAY MUSEUM No guided / visit on your own
No backpacks / Purses ok.
Housed in a breathtaking former railway station, the Musée d'Orsay is home to the world’s largest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces. You can walk among the vibrant works of Monet, Degas, Renoir, and Van Gogh, all while admiring the building's original Beaux-Arts architecture and massive station clocks. It offers a more intimate, color-filled experience than the sprawling Louvre.

Bus transfer to MONTMARTRE
Perched atop the highest hill in Paris, Montmartre is a charming village-like district that was once the playground of artists like Picasso and Dalí. At its summit sits the white-domed Sacré-Cœur Basilica, offering one of the most panoramic views of the entire city. Nearby, the Place du Tertre remains filled with painters and caricaturists, capturing the enduring creative spirit of the neighborhood.

FRAGONARD perfume museum 
1h visit
The Musée du Parfum Fragonard is a sensory treasure tucked inside a grand Napoleon III-style townhouse near the Opéra Garnier. This museum offers a captivating look at 3,000 years of fragrance history, guiding visitors past antique copper stills and rare bottles that reveal the secrets of the master "nose." The immersive experience concludes with a curated shopping opportunity, allowing you to browse the Maison’s exclusive collection of perfumes, soaps, and candles at direct-from-factory prices.

OPERA GARNIER with our licensed local guide
No backpacks / Purses ok. 1h30 visit
The Opéra Garnier is a dazzling display of Second Empire luxury, featuring a grand staircase of white marble and a stunning auditorium crowned by a ceiling painted by Marc Chagall. As the primary setting for The Phantom of the Opera, the building is shrouded in mystery and opulence. Every corner of the interior is adorned with gold leaf, velvet, and intricate carvings that rival any royal palace.

GIVERNY MONET HOUSE with guide Valérie
Giverny is the picturesque village where Impressionist painter Claude Monet lived and worked for 43 years. You can walk through the vibrant flower gardens and visit the famous water garden, complete with the Japanese bridge and water lilies that inspired his most iconic paintings. The site feels like a living canvas, preserved to look exactly as it did when the artist lived there.

INVALIDES - No guided / visit on your own 
https://www.musee-armee.fr/plan-interactif/
Recognizable by its magnificent golden dome, Les Invalides was originally built by Louis XIV as a hospital and retirement home for war veterans. Today, it houses the Musée de l'Armée and serves as the final resting place of Napoleon Bonaparte. The complex is a powerful monument to France’s military history, blending somber memorials with grand architectural design.
